proposed.explanation:
RANKING BY P/E RATIO (cheapest first):
1. ABUK (Abu Qir): ~6.5× (annualised from 9M EPS of 8.74 EGP; price 76.21)
2. EFID (Edita): 9.4× (price 20.40 / FY25 EPS 2.18)
3. TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): 11.8× (price 82.50 / FY25 EPS 6.98)
4. ETEL (Telecom Egypt): 11.9× (price 141.95 / FY25 EPS 11.93)

RANKING BY EPS GROWTH (highest first):
1. ETEL: +149% (4.79 → 11.93)
2. ABUK: +104% (4.28 → 8.74, 9M YoY)
3. EFID: +100% (1.09 → 2.18)
4. TMGH: +59% (4.38 → 6.98)

IMPORTANT CAVEATS:
• ETEL: Net profit fell from 10,111,328,000 EGP (FY24) to 578,063,000 EGP (FY25), a 94% decline, yet EPS rose 149%. This implies a ~98% reduction in shares outstanding, which is highly unusual. The 2024 figure may include a one-time gain (e.g., asset disposal). This inconsistency makes ETEL's earnings quality uncertain; I have weighted it lowest in the allocation.
• ABUK: Only 9-month (Jan–Sep 2026) data is available; the P/E is annualised (×4/3), which assumes the second half matches the first. Full-year FY2026 results are not yet in the evidence.
• TMGH and EFID: Full-year FY2025 data, consistent between net profit and EPS growth. Most reliable for comparison.

RECOMMENDED 4-STOCK ALLOCATION (100,000 EGP):
• EFID – 1,470 shares × 20.40 = 29,988 EGP (~30%)
• TMGH – 363 shares × 82.50 = 29,947.50 EGP (~30%)
• ABUK – 328 shares × 76.21 = 24,996.88 EGP (~25%)
• ETEL – 105 shares × 141.95 = 14,904.75 EGP (~15%)
Total invested: 99,837.13 EGP; residual cash: 162.87 EGP.

Rationale: EFID and TMGH get the largest weights because they have full-year, internally consistent data, solid double-digit growth, and P/E below 12×. ABUK is attractive on valuation (cheapest P/E) and strong 9M growth, but the shorter reporting window adds uncertainty. ETEL is included for diversification and its low P/E, but the 15% cap reflects the data inconsistency risk.

RISKS: All four stocks are Egyptian-listed and subject to currency, regulatory, and macroeconomic risk. Past growth does not guarantee future performance. The ETEL profit collapse (if not a one-time item) could signal structural weakness. ABUK's annualised P/E may be optimistic if H2 slows. With a 7+ year horizon and medium risk tolerance, this diversified 4-stock basket is appropriate, but you should review holdings annually and be prepared for 20–30% drawdowns in any single name.

final.explanation:
CORRECTION FROM PREVIOUS RECOMMENDATION:
In my prior answer I misread the ETEL net-profit row. The figure 22,578,063 (in thousands) is the FY2025 value, not a note number. The correct ETEL net profit is 22,578,063,000 EGP for FY2025, not 578,063,000. This changes ETEL's story dramatically: profit GREW 123% year-on-year (10.1 B → 22.6 B EGP), and the modest gap between profit growth (+123%) and EPS growth (+149%) implies only a ~10% reduction in shares outstanding (plausible buyback), not the 98% collapse I previously flagged. ETEL is now the strongest grower in the set with internally consistent data.

RANKING BY P/E RATIO (cheapest first):
1. ABUK (Abu Qir): ~6.5× (annualised from 9M EPS 8.74 × 4/3 = 11.65; price 76.21)
2. EFID (Edita): 9.4× (price 20.40 / FY25 EPS 2.18)
3. TMGH (Talaat Moustafa): 11.8× (price 82.50 / FY25 EPS 6.98)
4. ETEL (Telecom Egypt): 11.9× (price 141.95 / FY25 EPS 11.93)

RANKING BY EPS GROWTH (highest first):
1. ETEL: +149% (4.79 → 11.93, FY24→FY25)
2. ABUK: +104% (4.28 → 8.74, 9M YoY)
3. EFID: +100% (1.09 → 2.18, FY24→FY25)
4. TMGH: +59% (4.38 → 6.98, FY24→FY25)

RANKING BY NET-PROFIT GROWTH (highest first):
1. ETEL: +123% (10,111,328,000 → 22,578,063,000 EGP)
2. EFID: +68% (1,606,727,698 → 2,695,301,670 EGP)
3. TMGH: +43% (12,769,517,325 → 18,201,981,482 EGP)
4. ABUK: N/A (only 9-month data; no full-year comparison available)

RECOMMENDED 4-STOCK ALLOCATION (100,000 EGP):
• EFID – 1,470 shares × 20.40 = 29,988.00 EGP (~30%)
• ETEL – 211 shares × 141.95 = 29,951.45 EGP (~30%)
• TMGH – 242 shares × 82.50 = 19,965.00 EGP (~20%)
• ABUK – 262 shares × 76.21 = 19,967.02 EGP (~20%)
Total invested: 99,871.47 EGP; residual cash: 128.53 EGP.

Rationale:
• ETEL and EFID receive the largest weights (30% each). ETEL now shows the strongest and most coherent growth story (profit +123%, EPS +149%, P/E 11.9×). EFID offers the best P/E among full-year companies (9.4×) with 100% EPS growth.
• TMGH (20%) provides a large-cap, moderate-growth anchor (P/E 11.8×, profit +43%).
• ABUK (20%) is the cheapest on P/E (~6.5×) with strong 9M EPS growth (+104%), but the shorter reporting window (9 months, not full year) warrants a slightly smaller weight.

RISKS AND CAVEATS:
• ABUK P/E is annualised (×4/3); actual FY2026 EPS may differ if H2 slows.
• All four are Egyptian-listed; EGP currency risk, regulatory changes, and macro factors are not captured in these figures.
• Past growth does not guarantee future performance. With a 7+ year horizon and medium risk tolerance, this diversified basket is appropriate, but expect 20–30% drawdowns in any single name.
